skin.setting: a grand alpine hotel closed for the off-season, 1968
skin.title: Snowbound at the Berghof
skin.place: The Grand Hotel Edelweiss, high in the Swiss Alps
skin.styleGuide: Moody cinematic 35mm film photography, cool winter palette, dim amber tungsten lighting, frost on glass, velvet upholstery, 1960s tailored fashion.

rooms.name: the billiard room
rooms.description: A wood-paneled retreat with green baize tables draped in dust sheets.

rooms.name: the reception hall
rooms.description: The imposing front desk beneath heavy brass chandeliers and key racks.

rooms.name: the solarium
rooms.description: A glass-walled gallery overlooking frozen pine valleys and drifting snow.

rooms.name: the ski lounge
rooms.description: A rustic hearthside chamber adorned with vintage skis and mounted antlers.

rooms.name: the cloakroom
rooms.description: A narrow corridor lined with numbered cedar pegs and heavy fur wraps.

rooms.name: the grand salon
rooms.description: A vast ballroom featuring towering stone fireplaces and ornate rugs.

rooms.name: the snow terrace
rooms.description: A sweeping outdoor stone promenade exposed to the biting Alpine wind.

people.name: Arthur Vance
people.bio: A weathered mountaineer responsible for maintaining the shuttered resort through the cold months. He knows every hidden passage and creaking beam in the sprawling timber hotel.
people.voice: Gruff, low, and economical with words.
people.motive: Steiner had threatened to dismiss him without a pension over disputed inventory shortages.
people.portrait: A sturdy man in his late fifties with rugged features, salt-and-pepper hair, wearing a heavy cable-knit wool sweater.

people.name: Beatrix Von Berg
people.bio: A wealthy socialite who lingered past the seasonal closure to finalize estate paperwork. She carries herself with frosty elegance and expects absolute discretion.
people.motive: Steiner held promissory notes that would have bankrupted her family estate if called in.
people.portrait: An elegant woman in her forties with styled auburn hair, high cheekbones, wearing a tailored midnight-blue wool dress.

people.name: Claude Mercier
people.bio: A meticulous hotelier who has served the resort's wealthy patrons for over two decades. His polite demeanor masks a deep resentment of the hotel's ownership.
people.voice: Smooth, formal, and practiced in neutral diplomacy.
people.motive: Steiner had secretly finalized a deal to sell the hotel to a modern conglomerate, eliminating Claude's position.
people.portrait: A slender man in his fifties with neatly parted silver hair, wearing a crisp charcoal three-piece suit.

people.name: Dorothea Lind
people.bio: An efficient administrative assistant who managed Steiner's correspondence and private ledger. She observes everything quietly behind thick horn-rimmed spectacles.
people.motive: Steiner had recently discovered she was leaking financial audits to tax investigators.
people.portrait: A young woman in her late twenties with dark hair pinned in a neat chignon, wearing a pleated grey wool skirt suit.

people.name: Erich Kessler
people.bio: A celebrated modernist designer visiting to draft plans for upcoming seasonal renovations. He possesses an exacting eye for spatial symmetry and order.
people.motive: Steiner intended to scrap Kessler's life's work and demolish his signature alpine annex.
people.portrait: A tall, lean man in his thirties with sharp jawline, close-cropped dark hair, wearing a high-collared black turtleneck sweater.

people.name: Felix Steiner
people.bio: The autocratic proprietor whose ruthless business dealings made him numerous enemies. His body was found lifeless amidst the fresh powder on the open terrace.
people.portrait: A heavy-set man in his early sixties with thinning grey hair and a stern countenance, dressed in a velvet dinner jacket.

skin.briefing: A sudden blizzard has cut off the Grand Hotel Edelweiss from the valley below during its off-season closure. At midnight, hotel owner Felix Steiner was discovered dead on the snow terrace. Only five people remain trapped inside the frozen lodge, each with their own grievances and secrets. You must reconstruct their movements throughout the evening and unmask the killer.
skin.scene: A grand multi-story alpine hotel isolated on a snowy mountain ridge at dusk, illuminated only by warm light glowing through frosty panoramic windows into the gathering winter gloom.
skin.summingUp:
The frost is thick against the tall windows tonight, and the amber light in this room only sharpens what is already clear. Let us establish the exact hour Felix Steiner met his end. To begin with, the murder was not at five o'clock or eleven o'clock, because Card 5 narrows down when the murder happened. Next, the murder was not at eight o'clock, nine o'clock or ten o'clock, because Card 10 narrows down when the murder happened. Moving further, the murder was not at six o'clock, because Card 11 narrows down when the murder happened. That leaves seven o'clock as the only possible time.

From the hour, we turn to the place and the company kept there. Arthur Vance and Dorothea Lind are in the clear, because the killer and Felix Steiner were both in the snow terrace when it happened.

That brings us to the final truth among those who remain. Claude Mercier and Erich Kessler are in the clear, because there is no way for Beatrix Von Berg to have been innocent. Steiner held promissory notes that would have bankrupted her family estate if called in, and so, at seven o'clock out on the snow terrace, Beatrix Von Berg took his life.
